content:
Mao’s statement expresses the hope that through socialist transformation of agriculture, “all the rural people will become increasingly well off together.”  
The option that most directly undermines this hope is one where the policies meant to achieve this goal instead brought famine and poverty to the peasantry.  

Option (C) describes exactly that: cooperatives and the Great Leap Forward’s emphasis on rural steel production led to agricultural disruption and famine, contradicting Mao’s vision of shared prosperity.  

Final answer: (C)
